subject: Re: Redwood evaluation — observability & infra comparison / next tests
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Collins <avery@greenleaf.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood follow-up & suggested evaluation plan

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate the clear priorities you shared. Quick recap and a proposed next-steps plan so we stay aligned: 

Highlights from discovery
- Primary goal: deploy an inference endpoint for real-time personalization (latency-sensitive) and batch embedding pipelines.
- Top non-functional priorities: observability (per-route token breakdown, tracing), predictable p95 latency, and cost predictability vs hyperscalers.
- Compliance: SOC2 and data residency are gating items for procurement.

Proposed next tests (we can run these in a 2-week sandbox window):
1) Baseline latency & throughput: same prompt set on Redwood vs AWS Bedrock (selected models) — capture p50/p95/p99, token cost, and tail behavior under concurrency.
2) Streaming & partial-output behavior: measure time-to-first-token and steady-state throughput with streaming SDK.
3) Cache/warm-start test: KV/prefix cache warm vs cold to quantify token savings.
4) Observability checklist: per-request traces, per-token cost attribution, per-model/route dashboards, alerting hooks (PagerDuty/SNS), retention windows.

Attached is an evaluation-matrix-template.csv you can use to jot down requirements and grading criteria.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll loop in Vivek for a technical deep-dive to scope the tests (suggest Tue/Thu next week).
- Can you share the canonical prompt sample (~200–500 prompts) and a representative concurrency pattern?
- We’ll prepare a short comparison doc vs the hyperscalers and a demo of the Redwood Console observability dashboard.

If that sounds good I’ll schedule the deep-dive and send sandbox invites.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Avery Collins <avery@greenleaf.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@greenleaf.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Redwood follow-up & suggested evaluation plan

Sergio — thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Observability is the highest priority for our architecture team. We need examples of:
   - per-route token & cost breakdown (not just aggregated usage)
   - distributed tracing that ties a generated token back to a request ID and downstream app trace (OpenTelemetry preferred)
   - retention controls (how long logs/metrics are kept and export options)

2) Comparison vs hyperscalers: we’re running parallel tests with AWS Bedrock and Vertex AI. Cost and network egress are big factors — show us how Redwood’s cost-per-token and batching strategies change the economics.

3) Compliance: procurement needs SOC2 evidence and a short note on data residency options (US-only vs multi-region).

We can provide a 200-prompt sample and a small concurrency script. Can the sandbox capture the same telemetry as your hosted customers (i.e., Console dashboards + raw logs)?

Avery Collins
Director of ML Engineering, GreenLeaf Analytics
avery@greenleaf.ai
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 10:37:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Redwood follow-up & suggested evaluation plan

Laura / Vivek — forwarding Avery’s notes. Proposed internal plan and owner assignments: 

- Vivek: own the technical test harness and observability capture. Tasks: build the A/B harness to hit Redwood vs Bedrock (same prompts), instrument OpenTelemetry traces and per-token attribution, produce a small dashboard (Grafana/Console) with p50/p95/p99.
- Laura: lead commercial messaging for hyperscaler comparison and coordinate with procurement on SOC2 evidence & residency options.
- Sergio (me): timeline and customer comms, coordinate sandbox access and HubSpot updates.

Concrete deliverables for the customer: 
- Test harness repo + run instructions (private drive link).
- One-page comparison matrix (cost per 1M tokens, expected unit economics after batching/caching).
- Console demo user + a 30-min walkthrough.

Notes on observability: capture the following fields per request — request_id, route_name, model_variant, token_count, emitted_tokens, start_time, ttf_token (time-to-first-token), kernel_latency_ms, queue_wait_ms, and the OpenTelemetry trace id. We should also show how to export logs to S3/BigQuery.

I started a draft hyperscaler-comparison-draft.xlsx (attached) with quick numbers — needs validation. Vivek, tell me what you need for the prompts and concurrency shape.

Thanks — Sergio
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood follow-up & suggested evaluation plan

Got it — I’ll stand up the harness. Quick asks so I can size infra and instrumentation: 
- Please drop the 200-sample prompt set into the shared Drive link (or DM for secure upload).
- Concurrency profile: typical burst pattern (10s bursts to 200 concurrent for 30s, idle 5m) or steady 50 RPS? Which should we emulate first?
- Any compliance sandbox constraints (no PII)?

I’ll instrument traces with OpenTelemetry and push metrics to a demo Grafana as well as Redwood Console. I’ll include a runbook for reproducing the tests and a snippet to calculate per-token cost from our billing logs.

— Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Avery — appreciate the specificity. Short answers and next steps: 

- Sandbox telemetry: yes — the sandbox will surface the same Console dashboards and we’ll provide raw logs + OTEL traces for the A/B runs. Retention in the sandbox will be 7 days by default; we can extend to 90 days for procurement review on request.
- SOC2 & residency: certified SOC2 Type II report available (I’ve asked Laura to send the summary). We support region pinning for Hosted (US-only) and Private deployment options for stricter residency.
- Hyperscaler economics: we’ll publish a cost matrix showing raw per-token cost and an adjusted cost after batching/cache (what you asked for). Expect the initial draft by Wed.

Proposed timeline:
- Tue 10 Mar: technical deep-dive with Vivek (30–45 min) — goal: finalize harness and get sample prompts.
- Wed 11 Mar: we provide sandbox credentials and the comparison draft.
- Week of 16 Mar: run 3-day A/B test and share results + short 1-page exec summary.

Links / attachments:
- Redwood Console sample dashboard (attached: redwood-console-sample-dashboard.png)
- Shared drive with test harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleSharedDriveLink
- HubSpot deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/GL-2026-039
